section_summary: This section covers diplomatic reporting and internal State Department analysis regarding Japanese political, economic, diplomatic, and military affairs between October 1940 and February 1941. It contains the concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for October 1940 along with complete monthly lists of telegrams and despatches sent to Washington, an internal Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing December conditions, and Tokyo Despatch No. 5321 containing the December 1940 monthly report (Report No. 1671). Prominent subjects include the establishment and controversy surrounding the Imperial Rule Assistance Association and 'New National Structure', cabinet reorganizations, worsening United States-Japan relations over embargoes and China, Axis diplomacy under the Tripartite Pact, border tensions between Thailand and French Indochina, and expanding wartime economic controls.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for October 1940, covering internal politics, economic controls, bond issues, the sale of the Japan Advertiser, and Embassy telegram and despatch logs.
subfiles.summary: This concluding part of the Embassy's report on conditions in Japan for October 1940 covers the launch of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association under Count Yoriyasu Arima and Prince Konoye's public denials of communist tendencies within the 'new national structure'. It details domestic economic conditions including poor government bond absorption, record Bank of Japan note issuance, rationing of sugar and matches, small business relief programs, electricity shortages, and agricultural crop estimates. The narrative also notes the forced sale of the American-owned Japan Advertiser to the Japan Times and Mail, followed by complete registers of telegrams (Nos. 924-1083) and despatches (Nos. 5026-5105) transmitted by the Tokyo Embassy during October 1940.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of October, 1940 (Report No. 1670)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing significant political and economic items from Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5321 regarding Japan in December 1940.
subfiles.from: Herbert M. Fales, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 5321 (December 1940): planned Nanking central bank, growing German colony, Imperial Rule Assistance Association powers, steel output against American embargoes and halted industrial expansion.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo's Despatch 5321: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of December 1940

subfiles.about: Monthly diplomatic report from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reviewing Japanese foreign relations, domestic politics, military campaigns, and economic controls during December 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Despatch No. 5321 transmits Report No. 1671 detailing Japanese political, diplomatic, military, and economic developments during December 1940. It extensively analyzes American-Japanese friction, including Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka's speech to the America-Japan Society, Ambassador Grew's response, Japanese responses to diplomatic representations regarding American property and trade in China, and growing Japanese hostility over American loans to China and expanded export embargoes. The report also chronicles the arrival of German raider prizes at Kobe and British protests, the conclusion of the treaty with Wang Jingwei's Nanking regime, border clashes between Thailand and French Indochina, cabinet changes bringing Baron Hiranuma and General Yanagawa into key ministries, and contentious domestic debates surrounding the New National Structure and industrial control plans.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 5321: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of December, 1940 (Report No. 1671)
